title: Browser approval gates
summary: A recipe step typed operator_gate machine_browser_approval approves the installer's Match code in the test machine's own signed-in browser: Safari on macOS, the desktop Chromium on Linux and WSL. Every driver shares one matcher: only the installer-opened tab on the declared origin with the displayed code, revalidated before Approve machine is pressed, and only a same-origin navigation away from it counts. On Linux the gate requires /usr/bin/x-www-browser to resolve to a Chromium program, the same read the Machine QA provisioner verifies: the XFCE desktop opens links through exo-open, which falls back to debian-sensible-browser and runs x-www-browser, so this system-wide alternative, not mimeapps.list or xdg-settings, decides which browser opens. The provisioner installs Ubuntu's chromium-browser package, whose /usr/bin/chromium-browser script runs the snap, and selects it; a link straight to /snap/bin/chromium resolves to the snap launcher, which cannot run under the x-www-browser name, and refuses. The gate starts Chromium with a login shell's XDG_DATA_DIRS; an x-www-browser that is not Chromium refuses linux_desktop_default_browser_not_chromium. It then starts the desktop and Chromium with a loopback DevTools port and runs the installer on that desktop; the step always attaches a desktop screenshot. A host without a desktop refuses headless_linux_browser_approval_unavailable. A login shell that cannot print XDG_DATA_DIRS refuses linux_desktop_session_environment_unavailable. Both name the provisioning recovery. A setup that exits before or during approval fails the gate as terminal_setup_exited with its exit code and printed refusal, not as missing approval context. When the helper does not confirm the approval, the gate fails at once as machine_browser_approval_not_confirmed instead of waiting out gate_timeout_seconds; the helper's own code stays in browser_automation_error_code with a recovery. While it waits, each heartbeat prints a machine_qa.heartbeat line (phase operator_gate) that yoke watch qa-plan counts as progress; starting-state reset, fixture cleanup and restore print the same line on a background heartbeat. Safari confirms an in-place approval by the Machine connected heading, matched by value, name or title over one window walk per poll; a confirmation that never appears records observed_url, confirmation_wait_seconds and last_error. Approval coordinates use the shared MATCH_CODE_ALPHABET, MATCH_CODE_LENGTH and derived MATCH_CODE_PATTERN exported by yoke_contracts.machine_authorization: exactly four characters from 23456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ. The complete verification URI must contain exactly the displayed match code on the declared HTTPS origin, or on a declared loopback HTTP origin (a case that prepares the admission fixture declares its own server, which is how company sign-in approves the teammate's machine). The gate sends at most Enter before approving; the agent-mode setup driver opens the link itself with --open-link. Other code formats, mismatched codes, duplicate query values and unrelated origins refuse before browser approval. The gate's machine_qa.operator_gate line carries self_approving true: yoke watch qa-plan counts it as progress, and the code needs no action and is never forwarded.
